Method: Demonstration on clean Windows host with no Rust toolchain and no FFmpeg: download make_video_slideshow.exe (SR-023), run it so the first-run GUI wizard (SR-026) writes a valid config (SR-030) and the startup self-check (SR-024) fetches/locates FFmpeg (SR-027), then run build; assert a playable MP4 results and no documented end-user step installs Rust/requires a source checkout/edits .rs/requires hand-editing the config

Run validate end-to-end with all runtime prerequisites satisfied (FFmpeg on PATH, valid config, readable media_root, writable output base_dir) on a host with no Rust; assert one labeled plain-language pass/fail line per prereq and exit zero. Integration permutation only; the pass/fail aggregation->exit-code helper is unit-covered by TC-049

Run validate end-to-end with each essential prerequisite individually failed; assert that prereq's line reports fail and validate exits non-zero with no output. Integration permutation only; aggregation helper unit-covered by TC-049
Run build when an essential prerequisite fails (FFmpeg missing / unreadable media_root / unwritable output); assert build refuses to start, produces no output, exits non-zero
Load a config (TOML and JSON) that omits all optional fields; assert load succeeds using documented serde defaults and Config::validate passes
Inspect Quick Reference §4 and OutputDef/InputConfig/OutputConfig/ProcessingConfig structs: every user-facing field has a documented default and unit
Call Config::validate on configs with media_root-missing, empty outputs, zero dims, zero fps, crf>51; assert each is rejected with an InvalidConfig message
Run build over a media set; capture stderr/log; assert per-stage processed/total progress updates are emitted as work proceeds

On build success assert completion summary lists every written output path; on failure (no valid output) assert plain-language failure message and non-zero exit; assert any final output >3.5GB is listed with path+size
ffprobe a default-config output; assert codec=h264, container=mp4, pix_fmt=yuv420p, moov before mdat (faststart), width%2==0 and height%2==0, 24<=fps<=30
Parameters: codec=h264; container=mp4; pix_fmt=yuv420p; faststart=on; dims=even; fps=default

Construct OutputDef and assert total_frames/fade_frames derive from configured fps and timing (fps=30, 6s display, 0.5s fade -> 180 frames, 15 fade frames)

Method: ffprobe default-config and configured-fps outputs; assert default 24<=fps<=30 and configured fps is honored in the encoded stream
Encode identical input at each CRF; assert default quality_crf is within 26-30, the configured CRF is passed unchanged to libx264 (-crf), and lowering CRF increases output file size

Configure media whose estimated output exceeds 3.5GB; assert build emits a warning naming the output and pointing to mitigations, using duration = sum(clip durations) - transitions x fade_time_secs. Integration permutation only; the estimate/oversize math is unit-covered by TC-047
Produce a final output file >3.5GB; assert it is surfaced (path + size) in the completion summary. Integration permutation only; the oversize threshold predicate is unit-covered by TC-047
Hash every file under media_root before and after each operation, including a run interrupted mid-execution; assert all files byte-for-byte unchanged and none added/removed
Kill build before an output finalizes; assert no file with the final <name>.mp4 name exists (only a distinguishable temp artifact); re-run completes normally without double-producing or skipping
With FFmpeg absent from PATH, run validate and build; assert each prints an FFmpeg-not-found message with a fix hint, produces no output, exits non-zero
Drive FfmpegEncoder::finish on a child that exits non-zero; assert SlideshowError::Ffmpeg with the exit status is returned (no false success); assert write_frame propagates broken-pipe

Force a non-zero FFmpeg exit during an output; assert the error names the failing output/file, exits non-zero, lists no written file for that output, and terminates within a bounded time (no indefinite hang)
Build over a media set mixing some unreadable/unsupported files with valid files; assert each bad file is skipped, logged with path+reason, valid files still produce output
some-bad vs all-bad input: assert summary states the skipped count; with >=1 valid output the run exits zero; flag the all-skipped exit semantics (see finding)

Constrain the output volume and the temp volume so writes fail with a real ENOSPC/ERROR_DISK_FULL; assert an out-of-space message naming the path, non-zero exit, and no file left with the final output name. Integration permutation only (real full volume); the is_disk_full classification helper is unit-covered by TC-048
Trigger disk-full mid-encode; assert no finalized <name>.mp4 is left for the affected output (atomic finalize)

With output base_dir missing/read-only and media_root missing, pre-run and mid-run; assert the exact path and problem are named in plain language, non-zero exit, no panic/stack trace, no silently-discarded output
Provide N output definitions in one config; run one build; assert N distinct MP4s written and ffprobe confirms each output's resolution/fps match its definition
Call MediaLoader::is_ignored / scan with ignore patterns across case variants and file vs folder targets; assert matching paths are excluded case-insensitively and non-matching files included
Two ClipPlan::new builds over identical file path+config produce identical path-seeded zoom/pan/rotation; assert windows fit inside the prescaled image and prescaled covers output at max zoom
Expected: Satisfies SR-022 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test transform::tests::windows_fit_inside_prescaled_image, transform::tests::prescaled_covers_output_at_max_zoom

Method: Assert Ken Burns window aspect ratio matches the output aspect ratio within rounding tolerance (path-seeded, deterministic)
Expected: Satisfies SR-022 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test transform::tests::aspect_ratio_of_window_matches_output

Method: FrameRenderer::load + render_range on a synthesized image at configured dims; assert each rendered frame is exactly width*height*3 bytes (even dims honored end-to-end)
Expected: Satisfies SR-006 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test image::tests::frames_have_expected_raw_size

Method: Demonstration/CI: assert the CI release workflow (on a release tag) builds and publishes a make_video_slideshow.exe asset to GitHub Releases and that the published artifact bundles/contains no FFmpeg; then on a clean Windows host with NO Rust/build tools, download that make_video_slideshow.exe and run validate then build, using only the binary + an FFmpeg obtained per SR-027; assert a playable MP4 is produced and no .NET/Rust runtime install is required
Parameters: binary=make_video_slideshow.exe; built-by=ci-on-tag; source=github-releases; ffmpeg-bundled=no; host=clean-no-rust; command={validate,build}

Method: Launch make_video_slideshow.exe on a clean Windows host across the config-present x ffmpeg-present matrix in an interactive session; assert every launch runs a dependency self-check reporting in plain language whether FFmpeg is locatable, that when FFmpeg is missing it prompts to fetch/locate it (SR-027), that on first run with no config it launches the GUI wizard (SR-026) before proceeding, and that the self-check requires no Rust and runs on a clean host

Inspect README/Quick Reference: audio and bulk_video_time_min splitting are explicitly labeled not-implemented in the Rust engine and route to the PowerShell pipeline/workaround; no doc claims they work
Inspect docs: one canonical quick-reference (commands + recommended settings) exists, is linked from README, and recommended-settings values appear in exactly one location with others linking to it
Inspect README/roadmap/spec/quick-reference for conflicting restated constraint values; assert fps-range, crf-default, 3.5GB threshold, resolution-set are each stated once with no conflicts

Inspect README/quick-reference: End User (run) and Developer (build-from-source) paths are distinct labeled sections; the End User quick-start has zero Rust/cargo/compiler steps; Rust build instructions appear only under Developer

Demonstration: on first run with no config in an interactive session, launch make_video_slideshow.exe; assert the GUI wizard (PowerShell/WinForms) appears, collects source path, intermediary/temp path, frame defaults (resolution/fps/quality) and single-vs-multiple-frames, and on completion the run proceeds with the new config; assert the wizard appears only in interactive use (SR-028)

Call the pure build_config mapping on a set of wizard-collected values (no GUI); assert the produced Config serializes to TOML that parses via Config::from_file and passes Config::validate (SR-002/SR-003), each collected field landing in its documented config field; assert the single-frames choice yields one [[outputs]] and the multiple-frames choice yields multiple
Expected: Satisfies SR-026 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test setup::config_builder::tests::build_config_maps_wizard_values_to_valid_config (intended, OBJ3)

Method: Drive the FFmpeg auto-fetch/fallback across the three states; assert online-fetch downloads FFmpeg into a per-user dir without elevation, verifies it (SR-029) and then locates it for validate/build; assert offline-existing uses a user-supplied/configured FFmpeg path with no download; assert offline-none does not silently proceed but reports FFmpeg-unavailable in plain language and exits non-zero; assert no state requires administrator rights

Call the resolve_ffmpeg resolution-order helper with the binary present in each position; assert the documented precedence PATH/configured-existing first, then the per-user auto-fetch cache, then trigger a fetch (when interactive/permitted), returning the first resolved path with no duplicated probing
Expected: Satisfies SR-027 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test ffmpeg::resolve::tests::resolve_ffmpeg_follows_precedence (intended, OBJ3)

Method: Harness guardrail across interactive states; assert that a non-interactive invocation (--config <valid> or --non-interactive, or no attached console) runs validate/build to completion with NO GUI/prompt shown and no wait for input, that a non-interactive run lacking a usable config/dependency exits non-zero with a plain message rather than launching a GUI or blocking, and that under CI/no-console every invocation terminates within bounded time and never opens a dialog

Call the is_interactive predicate with TTY/attached-console present vs absent and with --non-interactive / --config <path> set; assert it returns false (never prompt/GUI) in every non-interactive/CI case so the gated wizard (LLR-029) and fetch prompt (LLR-031) are suppressed
Expected: Satisfies SR-028 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test setup::interaction::tests::is_interactive_false_when_noninteractive_or_ci (intended, OBJ3)

Method: Call verify_checksum on a fetched FFmpeg whose checksum matches the pinned/trusted value vs one that mismatches (or is missing/corrupt); assert the match case permits use and the mismatch case emits a plain-language integrity-failure message, never executes the suspect binary, and aborts non-zero; assert the pinned checksum is recorded in the binary/config, not fetched unauthenticated alongside the download
Expected: Satisfies SR-029 AcceptanceCriteria via cargo test setup::ffmpeg_fetch::tests::verify_checksum_match_proceeds_mismatch_aborts (intended, OBJ3)

Method: Call resolve_config_path with the exe's own directory writable vs read-only; assert the config is written beside the exe when writable and under %APPDATA% when read-only, that the chosen path is reported in plain language, and that a subsequent run re-reads from the same precedence (beside-exe first, then %APPDATA%) without re-prompting/re-running the wizard

Method: Call OutputDef::even_dims on odd, already-even, and degenerate (1x1) configured dimensions; assert each dimension is rounded down to even (x & !1) and never falls below the even minimum of 2, so odd values can never reach yuv420p ffmpeg. Method: Call estimate_output_bytes / is_oversize: assert the estimate scales linearly with duration, a lower CRF estimates a larger size, the oversize predicate is false at exactly 3.5GB and true one byte above, and a long low-CRF run is flagged oversize.
